ثَبْتٌ : see ثَابِتٌ. ―
-b2- Also A man firm, or steady, of heart; (S;) and so ثَبْتُ الجَنَانِ; (A, Msb, TA;) pl. ثُبْتٌ: (TA:) or a man who acts, or proceeds, [firmly, steadily,] deliberately, or leisurely, (A, Msb,) in his affairs: (Msb:) and a courageous horseman, (M, K, TA,) earnest in the charge; (TA;) as also ↓ ثَبِيتٌ : (M, K, TA:) both of which signify also intelligent, and possessing self-restraint; or seldom erring or making a mistake or committing a fault. (A, TA.) And ثَبْتُ المَقَامِ A man who does not quit his station, or abode. (M.) And ثَبْتُ القَدَمِ [Firm-footed;] one who makes no slip in contention, or in fight. (A, TA.) And ثَبْتُ الغَدَرِ A man firm, or steady, in fight, or in speech, or discourse: (M, L, TA:) or whose tongue makes no slip in contentions. (S, TA.) ―
-b3- See also ثَبَتٌ: ―
-b4- and ثَبِيتٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
